name: Discord moderation and community bots
title: Best Discord Moderation and Community Bots in 2026
summary_line: Discord bots for moderation, role menus, support tickets, events, giveaways and server stats, ranked for game communities.
definition: A Discord moderation and community bot is an application added to a server that automates chores such as filtering spam, banning rule breakers, handing out roles, running support tickets, scheduling events and counting members. Some bots do many of these jobs, while others do one, and most sell a premium tier.
intro: A Discord server for a game starts as a few friends and ends up needing rules, roles, a support queue and event reminders. Bots take over that work, but there are dozens to choose from and most pages say little about price. This ranking compares thirteen of them. We read each bot's site and premium page, compared the listed features, and did not run the bots ourselves. Statements about popularity or being the best are the vendor's, and we label them so. Placement reflects fit for a community manager at a studio or guild who needs moderation and roles first, then tickets, events and extras. Where a page loaded without readable text, we say what we could not see.

criteria.heading: Moderation and security depth
criteria.text: Spam, raids and abuse are the first problems on any growing server. We checked which bots list automod, anti-spam, logging or security tools and which leave moderation out. A bot that documents several tools in one place ranks higher than one that only names moderation in its title.

criteria.heading: Roles and onboarding
criteria.text: Players pick their game, platform or region, and a server stays tidy when roles are assigned automatically. We looked for reaction roles, auto roles and role rewards. Bots that combine these with logging let a small team run a server with fewer bots installed.

criteria.heading: Support, events and engagement
criteria.text: Studios use Discord for bug reports, appeals and scheduled play. We noted ticket bots, calendars with availability polls, giveaways, leveling and server stats, and ranked all-rounders above single-purpose tools unless the angle was exactly that specialty.

criteria.heading: Cost and transparency
criteria.text: Most bots here have a free tier and a paid premium. We recorded whether the site states a price, says it is free, or is open source, and we marked pages we could not read. A bot whose features cannot be verified ranks lower, since a manager cannot judge it before installing.

market_notes: Across the thirteen bots, one site says it is completely free (Sapphire), and two are open source (YAGPDB and GiveawayBot, which also list premium options). The other ten either mention a premium page or show nothing about cost. No bot among the thirteen shows a dollar amount in the text we could read, and six had premium or about pages that load through JavaScript with no readable text, so prices must be checked directly on each site.

The category splits into all-rounders and specialists. Carl-bot, Sapphire, Dyno, MEE6 and Arcane overlap heavily on moderation, roles and commands, and most servers run one of them. Specialists such as Ticket Tool, Sesh, Statbot and GiveawayBot add a single capability and are installed beside the all-rounder. The trade-off is bot count: each extra bot means another set of permissions to audit and another place to configure rules, so many managers prefer one broad bot plus one or two specialists.

how_to_choose.title: Write the three problems you have today
how_to_choose.text: List what hurts now: spam, unassigned roles, unanswered bug reports, missed event times. Match each to a feature. Spam points to Wick, Dyno or Carl-bot, roles to Carl-bot or Sapphire, reports to Ticket Tool, events to Sesh. Skip features you do not need yet, since every extra module adds settings that someone must maintain.

how_to_choose.title: Start with one all-rounder and test the free tier
how_to_choose.text: Install a single broad bot such as Carl-bot or Sapphire on a test server, set up roles and automod, and watch a week of real activity. Sapphire's site says it is completely free, so it is a low-risk trial. Only add a specialist once a real gap shows, and check each premium page before assuming a feature is free.

how_to_choose.title: Audit permissions and plan for hosting
how_to_choose.text: Give each bot only the permissions it needs, because a compromised or abandoned bot with admin rights is a risk. If you want control over where code runs, consider open-source options like YAGPDB, which the site says can be self-hosted. Keep a note of which bot does which job so a new moderator can find the settings quickly.

faqs.q: What is the best Discord moderation and community bot in 2026?
faqs.a: Carl-bot ranks first because it combines reaction roles, automod, logging and custom commands in one modular bot. Sapphire is better if you want a free broad bot with slash commands and scheduled messages, and Wick is better if security against raids is the main worry.

faqs.q: Is there a free all-in-one Discord bot?
faqs.a: Sapphire's site says the bot is completely free and lists slash commands, auto moderation, reaction roles, logging and scheduled messages. Open-source options such as YAGPDB can also be self-hosted. Confirm whether any limits apply before relying on a free tier for a large server.

Ticket Tool is the specialist, described as a highly customizable ticket bot for community support. It does not do moderation or roles, so most servers run it beside a general bot such as Carl-bot or Dyno.

faqs.q: How do I schedule events and raid nights?
faqs.a: Sesh is a calendar and event bot, and its site describes availability polls that help find a time when everyone is free. A Premium tier is listed, but we could not read its price, so check before enabling it for a big guild.

faqs.q: Do I need more than one bot?
faqs.a: Often yes. An all-rounder like Carl-bot, Dyno or Sapphire covers roles and moderation, then a specialist adds tickets, events, giveaways or stats. Each additional bot needs permissions and configuration, so add them only when a real need appears.

faqs.q: Are the claims of being the best bot reliable?
faqs.a: They are the vendors' own words. Ticket Tool calls itself the number one support bot, Arcane's title calls it the best bot and Tatsu cites more than 1,350,000 servers. We did not verify those figures, so judge each bot by the features listed rather than by the slogan.

The site title says it is a moderation bot, but its about and premium pages loaded without readable text, so we could not read a feature list or prices. A bot you cannot compare ranks lower until its documentation can be checked.

tools.name: Carl-bot
tools.tagline: Modular bot for reaction roles, automod and logs
tools.best_for: Role menus and logging on a growing server
tools.pricing: A premium page exists at carl.gg/premium, but its text is not rendered without JavaScript; no prices were read.
tools.summary: Covers the four jobs most game servers start with: self-assigned roles, automatic moderation, audit logs and custom commands.
tools.verdict: Carl-bot describes itself as fully customizable and modular, listing reaction roles, automod, logging and custom commands. Those four cover the usual first-week needs of a game server: letting players pick a game or region role, filtering spam, recording what moderators did and adding simple commands. It leads this page because it handles roles and moderation in one bot with a web dashboard, which keeps a small team from stacking several bots.
tools.weaknesses: The premium page loads its text through JavaScript, so we could not read prices or what premium adds. The facts do not mention tickets, calendar events or giveaways, so those need other bots.
tools.wrong_for: Skip it if your main need is a support ticket queue; Ticket Tool is built for that.

The Carl-bot site is titled Carl-bot Dashboard.

tools.name: Sapphire
tools.tagline: Free bot with slash commands, automod and scheduled messages
tools.best_for: Servers that want a broad toolkit at no cost
tools.pricing: The site says the bot is completely free.
tools.summary: The site says it is completely free and lists slash commands, auto moderation, reaction roles, logging and scheduled messages.
tools.verdict: Sapphire is the only bot here whose site says outright that it is completely free. Its feature list combines custom slash commands, buttons and select menus with auto moderation, reaction roles, logging and social notifications, and it supports scheduled and triggered automated messages. For a volunteer-run community with no budget, getting roles, moderation and announcements from one free bot is a strong deal, which earns the second spot.
tools.weaknesses: Free status is the vendor's own statement and the facts do not say whether limits apply. The facts mention no ticket system or event calendar, and a bot with this many features takes time to configure well.
tools.wrong_for: Wrong for a server that needs a ticket workflow; Ticket Tool handles that directly.

tools.verdict: Dyno describes itself as a feature-rich and modular bot with web configuration, moderation, anti-spam, auto roles and custom commands. A moderator who prefers a web page to chat commands can enable only the modules needed and leave the rest off. The site shows a Get Premium option and a Battle Pass, and names Swift Media Entertainment as the copyright holder. It takes third place for its moderation depth and dashboard.
tools.weaknesses: No prices were in the text we read for Premium or the Battle Pass, so cost is unclear. The facts do not mention tickets, events or giveaways, and modular bots can overlap with others already on your server.
tools.wrong_for: Not for a team wanting a calendar or giveaway tool; Sesh and Giveaway Bot do those narrower jobs.

tools.summary: Focused on moderation and security, with Premium and VIP plans offered on its premium page.
tools.verdict: Wick describes itself as the moderation and security bot, and its premium page offers Premium and VIP plans to boost a server, with the line to iron out your server and fully secure it. That narrower aim suits a community that has been targeted by spam or hostile joins and wants protection first, with fun features handled elsewhere. It ranks fourth because it concentrates on security, not on roles, events or tickets.
tools.weaknesses: No prices were read for the Premium and VIP plans. The facts list no leveling, roles, tickets or events, and give no detail on which security controls exist beyond the general description.
tools.wrong_for: Skip it if you need engagement features such as levels; MEE6 or Arcane list leveling.
